speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger; can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if they have been constant or intermittent?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sounds like a significant injury. Given the mechanism of injury and the location, I need to rule out a fracture or ligament tear; can you tell me if you heard or felt a "pop" at the time of the accident and if there is any bruising or deformity visible now?

REQUEST TEST: X-Ray Right Hand

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand shows no bone fractures or dislocations. Soft tissue swelling is noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (Extensor Tendon Injury). The patient's history of a football injury causing the finger to be pulled forcefully, combined with pain and swelling in the distal finger, is classic for this condition. The mention of "Pyelonephritis" is unrelated and likely a misstatement by the patient regarding their knee or hip, which can sometimes result in referred pain or confusion, but the primary issue here is the finger injury.

I will proceed with imaging to confirm the diagnosis and assess for any associated fractures.

REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray Right Hand

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
